criteria.note: The opening paragraph names the exact action and the exact character to look for (flip the package, scan for 밀), satisfying 'korean food label gluten' well inside 200 words.
Title is 39 chars plus the 20-char appended suffix (59 total), description is 153 chars, keyword tokens present in both, and no phrase is repeated verbatim between them.
Headings carry the argument on their own — a skim of Step 1–4 plus 'When the label can't answer' and 'Three Korea-specific gluten-label traps' delivers the whole method.
Six internal links across four target posts, each placed where the reader has just hit the limit of the current page (저글루텐 trap, soy sauce, flavour-by-flavour snack detail).

All five FAQ answers — the 19-item allergen list, the 무 글루텐 20mg/kg definition, the 저글루텐 gap, the rice trap, and the wheat/barley/rye vocabulary — are each established in the body and read as self-contained answers.

There are real first-hand traces — the rice-cracker failure, the Pocachip flavour pair, an explicit correction log — but no dates, store names, brands or quantities attached to the author's own encounters.
criteria.evidence_quote: Rice breads and rice snacks are where we've been caught most often by 밀가루 or 밀 전분 in the ingredients.

criteria.note: Korean terms are consistently romanised, thresholds are numeric (20mg/kg, 19 declared substances), and products are named precisely enough to check (포카칩 오리지널, Sempio 양조간장 501).
Primary regulatory sources and two manufacturer product pages are linked, with the MFDS standard given as 고시 제2025-60호, 29 August 2025 and manufacturer pages marked 'retrieved August 2026'.
The piece repeatedly states what its method cannot establish and carries no commercial links needing disclosure.

findings.quote: The snack that broke me of trusting the allergen line alone was a "rice" cracker: allergen line clean, but 밀 전분 sitting a few items up in the ingredients.
findings.why: This is the article's single strongest first-hand moment, but it carries no brand, no store, no month, and no photo — so it reads as an illustrative anecdote rather than a verifiable observation. Google's experience signal rewards specifics a reader could not have invented; everything else in the piece is regulation-reading and two cited manufacturer pages, which are expertise signals, not experience.
findings.fix: Name the cracker (brand + flavour), the chain and neighbourhood where you bought it, and the approximate month. Do the same for the 'caught most often by 밀가루 or 밀 전분' claim in the traps section — one named rice bread with a date turns a general warning into evidence.

findings.quote: Everything about what sits on convenience-store shelves is our own shopping in Seoul — first-hand, but not a survey, and not lab-tested.
findings.why: The methodology note is honest and good for trust, but it also concedes that the shelf observations are undocumented — no count of stores, no time window. A reader cannot gauge how broad the sample is.
findings.fix: Add scope in one clause: roughly how many stores/chains, over what period (e.g. 'GS25, CU and 7-Eleven in three Seoul districts, Jan–Aug 2026').

findings.quote: A: Flip the package and read the ingredient list (원재료명, wonjaeryomyeong). Korea's mandatory allergen list — set by 식품등의 표시·광고에 관한 법률 시행규칙, 별표 2 — includes wheat, so wheat shows up as 밀.
findings.why: Every claim in this answer is supported by the body, so it scores full marks, but at roughly 1,200 characters it packs five separate claims into one FAQ answer. Rich-result snippets truncate, and the part that survives may be the least useful.
findings.fix: Split the celiac/NCGS escalation and the 'gluten-free claim is self-declared' point into their own Q/A pairs, leaving answer 1 at two or three sentences that front-load the 밀 / 보리 / 호밀 distinction.

findings.quote: The substances the allergen line must declare are fixed by [식품등의 표시·광고에 관한 법률 시행규칙 별표 2](https://www.foodsafetykorea.go.kr/portal/board/boardDetail.do?menu_no=3120&menu_grp=MENU_NEW01&bbs_no=bbs001&ntctxt_no=1091412)
findings.why: The MFDS 고시 is cited with a precise number and date (고시 제2025-60호, 29 August 2025), but the 별표 2 link — which carries the load for the central 19-allergen and shared-facility claims — is repeated three times with no amendment date or retrieval date attached. Readers cannot tell which revision was read.
findings.fix: Attach the enforcement-rule amendment number and effective date to the first 별표 2 citation, plus a retrieval date, the same way the 고시 is handled.

criteria.note: Nearly every regulatory and product claim carries a link, a retrieval date, or an explicit first-person marker, but a couple of concrete assertions ride on citations that don't actually cover them.
criteria.evidence_quote: The **Onion flavour of the same brand declares 밀.**

criteria.note: Product names (포카칩 오리지널, 샘표 양조간장 501), the 20mg/kg figure, the 19-entry allergen count, and the 고시 number/date are all specific, checkable, and internally consistent between FAQ, table, and body.
The piece states plainly which claims come from the MFDS text and which from the authors' own Seoul shopping, and names the limits — not a survey, not lab-tested, package-in-hand overrides.

No absolute safety guarantee anywhere; celiac and NCGS are separated at every decision point, cross-contamination is given its own step with the 혼입 exception explained, and the closing line states exactly what a clean scan does not prove.
Regulation version and retrieval dates are given, and both amendment churn and manufacturer reformulation are explicitly flagged as reasons the piece may be stale by the time it is read.
Hangul terms, romanisations, and the 19-entry allergen list are correct, and the load-bearing fact — wheat mandatory, barley and rye not — is stated repeatedly and used to structure the method.
Reader gets the full allergen table to check against, direct links to the regulation, the 식품안전나라 database, and a copy-pasteable Korean question for the 소비자상담실 line.

findings.quote: The **Onion flavour of the same brand declares 밀.**
findings.why: The Orion citation immediately before it is scoped to 포카칩 오리지널 only; the onion-flavour claim — the half that carries the article's punchline — has no source of its own. The error direction is conservative (it tells a reader to avoid something), so no safety decision is endangered, but a bolded product-specific fact should be traceable.
findings.fix: Add the product-page link (or product code) for the onion flavour with its own retrieved-date, or mark it as read off a package the authors held: 'the onion bag we checked in August 2026 declared 밀'.

findings.quote: Korean manufacturers reformulate without redesigning the package.
findings.why: Stated flatly as an industry fact with neither a source nor the first-person marking used elsewhere in the piece ('we have found', 'our own shopping'). It is a conservative caution and cannot cause a reader to eat gluten, but it is the load-bearing justification for the 'Re-scan every time' rule and currently rests on nothing the reader can check.
findings.fix: Recast as observed experience ('we have twice found a snack that cleared the scan fail a month later on identical packaging') or cite an MFDS/industry note on reformulation and label-change practice.
